description: White as the morning it vanished from the king's stable. It allows no rider, but walks beside the lost.
lore: In life it was somebody's, and expensive, and one morning the stall stood empty with the door still bolted. That story is presumably still being told wrong in the living country. The truth is the ordinary one: it came the way everyone comes, [[lore/the_waking|woke in the meadow grass]], and has no idea it is supposed to be a wonder.

It will not be ridden and has never once made a fight of it. Put a saddle on and it stands patiently through the girth and the buckles; get a leg across and it simply walks out from under the whole arrangement and leaves you holding tack in an empty field. There is nothing there to argue with. Nothing was refused.

What it does instead is walk beside people who are lost — at the shoulder, at exactly their pace, for as long as it takes. Several have tried following it, on the reasonable assumption that a horse doing that must know a way, and been walked in a wide meandering circle back to their own footprints, because it was never leading. It goes where you go. All it does is see to it that a person alone in the dark is a person and a horse.

[[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]] sees it more than anyone. Somebody comes stumbling in out of the dark towards the meadow fire with a white horse at their shoulder, and at the edge of the light the horse stops, and turns, and goes back out. It will not come in to the warm. The one courtesy she has never managed to do is thank it.
gm_notes: Description adopted verbatim from the monsters agent. The reversal is the record: it is not a guide, it is company — following it gets you nowhere because it is following you. That makes it a kindness with nothing inside it able to intend one, which is the note to hold; do not let a later text turn it into a psychopomp or give it a destination. Its refusal of the fire is deliberate and unexplained. Art check: no tack, no horn, no glow — a plain pale horse.
